court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties took place on 01.04.2001 at Reddiyarpalayam Police Station, Pondicherry. The appellant filed a petition under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 to dissolve the marriage. The Family Court dismissed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking annulment to establish that the marriage was not valid due to coercion.
legal_principles.held: We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent. We have also gone through the pleadings, the evidence on record both documentary and oral recorded and impugned order passed by the Family Court.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking annulment must establish the alleged fear and cessation of that fear before approaching the court.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court has concluded that the marriage between the appellant and the respondent cannot be annulled as the appellant has not established by way of evidence of the alleged fear and cessation of alleged fear before approaching the Court in a petition under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

outcome.final_order: The impugned order dated 18.03.2011 passed by the Family Court was set aside.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
advising on appeal against Family Court order
assisting in drafting a judgment on divorce
